text: dsh-web-bridge（DSH 网页客户端）：为 DeepSeek Harness 的 web_search 接入可替换的网页搜索 provider。插件通过 ctx.web 注册，并提供 /web-provider 命令和设置开关。搜索可使用 Bing、DuckDuckGo、Marginalia、Brave Search，词法引擎无结果时可调用 Exa 语义搜索。支持 HTTP 优先并按需启动浏览器，也可选择仅 HTTP 或仅浏览器；返回链接、标题和摘要。适合希望在 DSH 中搜索公开网页的用户。无需 API key 或账号；查询会发送到所选搜索服务，浏览器模式需要本机兼容浏览器。

dsh-web-bridge connects DSH web_search to Bing, DuckDuckGo, Marginalia, and Brave, with Exa as semantic fallback. It registers a provider and supports HTTP, browser, or automatic fallback. Results include links, titles, and snippets. No key is required; queries go to the selected service.
想让 DSH 的 web_search 用公开搜索引擎查网页。
Can I switch DSH web search to Bing or DuckDuckGo without configuring an API key?
I want DSH to search the public web with an optional browser fallback.
dsh-web-bridge 的功能「网页搜索 provider」：把 DSH web_search 请求交给配置的搜索引擎，并将结果整理成链接、标题和摘要。可选择 HTTP、浏览器或自动回退模式。
dsh-web-bridge 的功能「provider 切换命令」：注册 /web-provider 命令，可查看状态并在桥接 provider 与官方 provider 之间切换或探测。
dsh-web-bridge 使用前须知：搜索查询会发送到所选的公开搜索引擎；配置包含 Bing、DuckDuckGo、Brave、Marginalia，词法搜索无结果时还可能调用 Exa。

dsh-web-bridge README · dsh-web-bridge：Free web search for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), as a `ctx.web` provider.

**No API key. No account. No quota. No Docker.** It drives the browser you already have (or plain HTTP), reads the results page, and hands the seam a normal `WebSearchResult`.

dsh-web-bridge README · dsh-web-bridge：The built-in `deepseek-official` provider bills every search against your DeepSeek balance. When that balance is empty, `web_search` fails with `HTTP 402 Insufficient Balance` and the model is left improvising with `web_fetch`. This plugin exists to replace that path.

dsh-web-bridge README · Why another one：There are hundreds of `dsh-web-search-*` packages. The honest comparison:

| | Requires a key | Requires Docker | Requires a LAN service | Drives a real browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-official` (built in) | yes (balance) | no | no | no |
| Tavily / Brave / Exa / Serper backends | **yes** | no | no | no |
| SearXNG backends | no | **yes** | yes | no |
| **dsh-web-bridge** | **no** | **no** | **no** | yes, optional |

dsh-web-bridge README · Why another one：The trade is explicit: a key-based provider gives you ranked, aggregated results; this one gives you **whatever a public search page shows**, at zero cost. If you need semantic ranking, use a keyed provider. If you need search to keep working when the balance does not, this is the other side of the trade.

It is not a metasearch engine. It picks one engine, tries HTTP first, and only launches a browser when the HTTP page yields nothing usable.

dsh-web-bridge README · Measured behaviour：Verified on Windows 11 with Brave 155, DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. These are observations on one network from one region — treat them as a starting point, not a guarantee:

dsh-web-bridge README · Measured behaviour：| Engine | HTTP | Browser (headless) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Bing** | works | works | 15 destination URLs extracted per page; most reliable here |
| **DuckDuckGo** (HTML) | works, sometimes captcha | shell only | captcha appears under load |
| **Marginalia** | works | — | small independent index; few but clean results |
| **Brave Search** | challenge | challenge | needs a session cookie; off by default |
| **Exa** (semantic) | API | — | last resort, only when every lexical engine returns nothing |
| Google | blocked | renders, 0 extractable URLs | not supported |

dsh-web-bridge README · Why a semantic engine, and why last：The lexical engines match words. Ask for "Gemini Argon" when the documents say "Gemini 4 Argon" and DuckDuckGo returns *nothing* — the tokens do not overlap, so there is no match to rank. Measured directly: the same query with the `4` returned four results, without it zero.
section: Why a semantic engine, and why last

text:
dsh-web-bridge README · Why a semantic engine, and why last：Exa ranks by meaning, so the vague question still finds the page. It is the only keyless semantic source that works from here: public SearXNG instances now answer `403` or HTML where JSON was expected, and OpenAlex only indexes papers.

It runs **last**, after every lexical attempt, for two measured reasons:

- **Latency.** 1.5–5.6 s per call against ~1 s for a lexical engine.
- **Rate.** Five concurrent calls produced two `429`s; spacing them 3 s apart produced none.
section: Why a semantic engine, and why last

text:
dsh-web-bridge README · Why a semantic engine, and why last：The endpoint is serialised by an internal mutex, and a `429` is reported as `WEB_RATE_LIMITED`, never as an empty result — a rejected call returns a non-JSON body that would otherwise read as "nothing found". Repeated failures put the engine in the same cooldown a failing lexical engine gets.

No API key, no account, no cost. The public endpoint is a courtesy service with no SLA; if it disappears, the lexical path keeps working unchanged.
section: Why a semantic engine, and why last

text: dsh-web-bridge README · Why a semantic engine, and why last：`memo.json` remembers which engine/transport pair actually returned results on your machine and prefers it, so the plugin adapts instead of hardcoding one engine.

text:
dsh-web-bridge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-web-bridge
```

Then point the seam at it in that profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: bridge
    fetchProvider: http

`fetchProvider: http` matters: with two usable fetch providers and no pin, `web_fetch` fails with an ambiguity error.

dsh-web-bridge README · Install：**Restart after installing.** The set of mounted entries is composed at boot (`cordis.yml`) and is not recomputed later. Changing the *config* of an entry that is already mounted does apply live; adding one does not.

If your profile does not pick up the bundle patch — it happens on Windows Electron builds — declare the entry explicitly instead:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: web-bridge
      name: dsh-web-bridge
      config:
dsh-web-bridge README · Install：A bare `- id: web-bridge` at the top level only *patches* an entry that already exists; it does not create one.

dsh-web-bridge README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `providerId` | `bridge` | id this provider registers under; the `web` entry pins it |
| `engine` | `auto` | `auto`, or one of `bing` `duckduckgo` `marginalia` `brave` |
| `mode` | `auto` | `light` (HTTP only, never spawns a process) · `auto` (HTTP first, browser if empty) · `browser` |
| `channel` | `auto` | which browser to drive: `auto` `brave` `edge` `chrome` |
| `executablePath` | — | explicit browser binary, overrides `channel` |
| `headless` | `true` | keep the window hidden |
| `idleCloseMs` | `45000` | close the browser after this much quiet |
| `userDataDir` | — | persistent browser profile; omit for a throwaway one |
| `maxResults` | `8` | upper bound on returned sources |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | per-search deadline |
| `fallbackEngines` | `[]` | extra engines tried when the primary yields nothing |
| `provenance` | `true` | prepend one line naming engine and transport |
| `useBridge` | `true` | settings checkbox that flips the seam between this and `deepseek-official` |

dsh-web-bridge README · The browser is optional：`mode: light` never launches a process. In `auto`, every HTTP attempt across every candidate engine runs before the first browser is spawned, so a machine where HTTP works never pays for Chromium at all. Measured cost when a browser *is* used: 6 processes and ~410 MB while alive, 0 after it closes.

dsh-web-bridge README · Tools：The `tools/` directory is the part that makes failures diagnosable instead of mysterious.

```sh
node tools/env-doctor.mjs        # is each installed plugin compatible with THIS runtime?
node tools/preflight.mjs         # is the profile ready? run before restarting
node tools/rollback.mjs          # switch provider without DSH, if the plugin cannot load
node tools/selftest.mjs          # end-to-end search against live engines

dsh-web-bridge README · Tools：`env-doctor` exists because `dsh --dump-config` cannot see one thing: the **plugin manager's compatibility gate**, which only runs inside Electron. A plugin with a peer pinned to an older version is silently vetoed — installable, declared, importable, and never mounted. `env-doctor` reimplements that gate from the host's own rules.

dsh-web-bridge README · What this plugin does not do：- **No ranking or aggregation.** One engine per search, no merging of several result sets.
- **No JS-rendered pages** in `light` mode. That is what the browser mode is for.
- **No authenticated content.** Paywalls, logins and social platforms are out of reach.
- **No proxy support.**
- **Not a `web_fetch` replacement.** It pins `fetchProvider: http`, which is a different provider.
section: What this plugin does not do
